steps_unproved: D1 THE PROOFS FIRST, both plain scripts in the FAILURES/ok() pattern (no pytest), run bare with python3, committed and run RED before any build file exists. cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_beat_probes.py builds a temp folder with probes/ holding stub modules, each with a PROBE = Probe(...): 'standing' (trigger always True), 'chatty' (trigger True, while_true=True), 'broken' (trigger raises RuntimeError), 'done' (trigger True, enough returns True), 'needs_bus' (trigger returns context.get('bus') is not None); a stub bus class with post(**kw) that records the call and returns {'id': 'env-N'} and flush() that counts and returns {'flushed': n}. Teeth: (a) standing fires once across two beats and is held 'still true' on the second; (b) chatty fires on both beats; (c) broken is a fired entry with outcome 'refused' and the others still fire; (d) done fires once with 'cleared' and on beat two is held with a reason starting 'cleared'; (e) a name with no module lands in record['missing'] and nothing raises; (f) needs_bus fires, because the firer seeds context['bus']; (g) flush is called once per beat and its return is record['flush']; (h) a bus given as a zero-arg callable is called on the first beat only, never at construction. cairn/devices/cairn/proofs/test_groundloop_pulse.py carries the falsifier's teeth (1)-(4).

D2 cairn/tools/base/beat_probes.py imports NOTHING from cairn.tools.bus_client or any device (cairn/tools/base is a gate by the determinism walk and may not reach an oracle; bus_client imports inference_domain). API: class BeatProbes(device_id: str, folder: Path, names: list[str], bus=None). names is kept as a tuple (roster()). bus is a bus object (has post) or a zero-arg callable returning one, resolved on the first on_pulse and kept; None records every fire as 'unwired' (BaseShim._fire's own behaviour). bind(bus) replaces it. Loading: <folder>/probes/<name>.py via importlib.util.spec_from_file_location under the synthetic name 'cairn._beat_probe.<device_id>.<name>', held against its st_mtime and re-loaded when it changes; module.PROBE must be a cairn.tools.base.probe.Probe or the name is missing with the reason. Firing: a private class _Firer(BaseShim) whose device_id is the given id and whose probes() returns the loaded list; its __init__ sets self._delivery_wired = True because the firer is not the device's shim and receives no mail. on_pulse(now, context=None) -> dict: context = context if a dict else {}; context.setdefault('bus', bus) when bus is not None; record = firer.on_pulse(now, context); record['missing'] = [{'name', 'reason'}]; then if the bus has flush, record['flush'] = bus.flush() (an exception becomes record['flush'] = {'error': '<Type>: <msg>'}, never raised). The heartbeat holds the pulse module, so a module-level BeatProbes keeps crossing memory between beats.

D3 cairn/devices/cairn/groundloop/pulse.py: NAMES = ('history_integrity', 'trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles'); FIRER = BeatProbes('cairn', Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent, list(NAMES), bus=_bus) where _bus() does 'from cairn.tools.bus_client import reach; return reach("trouble")' — reach, not connect_bus: connect_bus off the runner roster reds cairn/tools/bus_client/probes/a_client_reaches_and_never_beats.py, and the trouble panel probe asks the trouble lane over the bus, so trouble's shim must be wired on it; on_pulse(now, context=None) returns FIRER.on_pulse(now, context). Proof tooth (4) calls FIRER.bind(stub) before on_pulse so no real bus is built in the proof.

D4 LIVE: after the build commit, the running heartbeat finds the new pulse site on its next beat (pulse_sites walks every beat); read ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/ground_loop/liveness.json on three consecutive beats: the trigger entry with device_id 'cairn' and level 'class' has ok true and its result carries fired+held naming both probes.

The pattern is concrete in cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_beat_probes.py and cairn/devices/cairn/proofs/test_groundloop_pulse.py (committed red at e4f714f3): module-level FAILURES list; ok(name, passed, detail) prints '  ok   <name>' or '  RED  <name>' and appends to FAILURES on a fail, never raising; main() runs every tooth, prints the verdict, and returns 1 if FAILURES else 0; the script exits with main()'s return. Tooth names are the PROVES dict's values, printed verbatim.
